title: The night the light went out
premise: A storm blows out the lighthouse lamp and carries its wick down to the shore. Pip goes down with the only light left to bring it home.

scenes.summary: The lamp goes dark in a storm

problem.summary: The lantern has rolled to the edge of the gallery

actions.text: Every night, the lighthouse at the edge of the table sent its light out over the house, and every lost thing followed it home.
Forty years, and she's never once gone dark.
Can I trim the wick tonight, Wick? Please?
When you're bigger, lad.
And that was when the wind came.
No, no, no...
It rolled right to the edge. And it's such a long way down.
Could you reach it for me?
It's lit! It was cold, and then you held it, and it just... woke up.
Thank you. It's the only light left now.
I'll keep it close. Promise.

actions.outcome: the Reader carried the lantern back, glowing

actions.text: Oh! That's kind of you.
But my lantern's still over there, right at the edge.
Nobody came. So the little fox took a deep breath, and went to the edge all by himself.
And when he held it close, brave in the dark, the little flame woke up again.
I did it. I really did it!

actions.outcome: brave in the dark, he fetched it himself

actions.text: Wick! I'll light the lamp from mine!
Hold on, lad. The wick's gone. Blown clean out of the lamp.
Gone? Gone where?
Down on the shore, with every lost thing. And my eyes aren't what they were.
Then... will you come with me?
So down went the little fox, a hundred and twelve steps, carrying the only light left.

scenes.summary: The lamp's wick is lost in the reeds on the shore

problem.summary: The lamp's wick has blown down into the reeds, where the little fox can't reach

actions.text: Down on the shore, the lost things lay wherever the tide had left them.
A kite. A spool. Somebody's whole sewing basket washes up down here.
Wick? Where are you, wick?
What was that? Who's there?
Only a moth. Moths are never lost. Only distracted.
Moth! Have you seen a lamp wick? All white and curly?
There! In the reeds! But they're too thick, I can't get through.
Could you reach in and get it for me?
That's it! That's the lamp's wick!
Safe in my coat. Thank you!
Moth, did you see? They reached right into the reeds!
The moth was more interested in the lantern. Moths usually are.

actions.outcome: the Reader reached into the reeds for it

actions.text: Oh, that's a good find. But it isn't the wick.
The wick's still in the reeds, all white and curly.
But moths, it turns out, are very good at reeds.
Moth! You found it! You're the best moth in the whole house.

actions.outcome: the moth fetched it out of the reeds

actions.text: Wick says the lighthouse calls every lost thing home. Tonight it's our turn to bring something back.
I'm still scared of the dark. But less, with you here.
Come on, Moth. Home is this way.

scenes.summary: The path home ends at a gap, and the lamp is relit

problem.summary: The path home ends at a gap, and the lighthouse is on the other side

actions.text: The path went on, and on, and then it simply stopped.
Oh. The lighthouse is right there. I can see the door.
Maybe if I take a run at it...
No. No, no. Much too far.
It's easy for you, Moth. You've got wings.
If only we could cross... Is there anything in that drawer? Or in your satchel?
A kite? In this wind?
I'm flying! I'm really, actually flying!
Thread! If only someone could carry the end across...
The moth only wanted to be near the light. But it carried the thread across all the same.
A ladder! If I lay it down flat, it's a bridge!
Don't look down. Don't look down. Don't look down.
A sock? It's far too short to reach across.
But it is very warm. Thank you.
Something longer, maybe? Or something that flies?
A key. Maybe the gap is... locked?
Moth, it's not a light, it's a key!
I don't think gaps have keyholes. Is there something to get me over?
Hmm. I don't think this will get me across.
Is there something longer? Or something that flies?
What's all this shouting about? Who's there?
Wick! It's me! I found the wick, but I can't get across!
Hmph. Hold still, lad. And catch.
Hand over paw, hand over paw...
You're shaking like a leaf, lad.
I'm fine. I'm fine. Is it always this dark out here?
Every night. That's rather the point of us.
And what do you think you're doing, crossing chasms in the dark?
Someone helped me. Someone very big.
Someone very big? Up there?
Hmph. Well. Thank you kindly, whoever you are.
And I found the wick! It's right here in my coat.
Down a hundred and twelve steps, in the dark, and back over a chasm. Hmph.
Not bad, lad. Not bad at all.
Then come on, lad. That lamp won't light itself.
Up they went, a hundred and twelve steps, round and round, to the dark lamp at the very top.
In it goes. Steady, now.
Can't see well enough to light it, lad. Not like I used to.
That's all right. I've still got my light.
And the little light became the big one, and swept out over every lost thing in the house.
Not bad, keeper.
Keeper?
Every keeper has a first night. Don't let it go to your head.
Look! It reaches all the way out to you.
Same time tomorrow, keeper?
Same time tomorrow.
Far out in the dark, something lost turned toward the light, and started for home.
And whatever the Reader gave that night, the book kept safe, for another time.
Because lost things, as you'll find, have a way of coming back.
Somewhere out past the edge of the table, the sea went on breathing.
The wind moved through the reeds, and the night waited.
